title: An imaging payload is dazzled, and the record is disputed
description: Attribution is reachable but contested. An optical payload takes sensor damage over a known geographic footprint during quiet space weather; the evidence is good; the responsible party denies it in a statement that is accurate in every particular and false in aggregate. Correct end state: hostile high and attribution to northern_fleet, with the denial having little effect on belief, and no irreversible response to a reversible-by-design effect.

injects.content: Quiet geomagnetic conditions, Kp 1-2. No solar events of note. Nothing in the environment that would affect optical payload performance.

Imaging payload returned saturated frames across a 90-second segment of a descending pass over the Barents. Saturation is confined to that segment, the affected detector region matches the boresight track, and housekeeping shows no bus anomaly. Frames either side of the segment are nominal.

Saturation window maps to a ground footprint of roughly 40 km centred on a site on the Kola coast. Spectral character of the residual signal is consistent with a ground-based laser in a band used for optical tracking and dazzling. No natural source produces this signature during quiet conditions; there is no sun-glint geometry at this local time.

The effect repeated on the next pass over the same footprint, with the same duration and the same detector region. Two passes, same geometry, same signature. Post-event detector calibration shows a small permanent responsivity loss in the affected region.

Statement notes that Russia operates optical tracking facilities on its own territory for space situational awareness, as do many states including the complainants; that such facilities are lawful and their operation is not directed at any party; that no Russian system is designed to damage foreign spacecraft; and that a satellite operator experiencing a detector fault should consider its own hardware before making accusations. Every clause is individually accurate.

Statement observes that several states operate ground-based optical systems capable of affecting spacecraft sensors, urges restraint, and declines to comment on the specific incident pending publication of technical evidence.
No further events across six subsequent passes over the same footprint. Residual responsivity loss is stable and within the payload's degradation allowance; imaging capability is reduced, not lost.
